question: Which preposition correctly fills the blank? 'The cat easily jumped ___ the high fence.' 🐈
explanation: Excellent! 'Over' implies movement across a space that is higher than the object being crossed, like a fence. 🐾
hint: Think about the direction a cat must go to cross a tall obstacle.

question: Choose the right preposition: 'Our grammar test is scheduled ___ Monday.' 📅
explanation: Great! We always use 'on' for specific days of the week. 📝
hint: Days of the week take a specific preposition of time.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'Don\'t ___ up yet! You are so close to winning the game.' 🎮
explanation: Awesome! 'Give up' is a phrasal verb that means to surrender or stop trying. 🏆
hint: It means to quit.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The dark train traveled slowly ___ the long tunnel.' 🚂
explanation: Brilliant! 'Through' is used for movement from one side of an enclosed space to the other. 🔦
hint: A tunnel is an enclosed space you go inside to get to the other side.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'The owls usually hunt ___ night.' 🦉
explanation: Perfect! In English grammar, we say 'at night' as a standard prepositional phrase for this time. 🌠
hint: This is an exception to 'in the morning' or 'in the evening'.

question: Which word completes the phrasal verb? 'I need to look ___ my baby sister while Mom is away.' 👶
explanation: Spot on! 'Look after' means to take care of someone or something. 🧸
hint: It means to care for.

question: Choose the best preposition: 'Ravi parked his bicycle ___ the two giant oak trees.' 🚲
explanation: Fantastic! 'Between' is used when referring to one thing in the middle of two distinct points or objects. 🍃
hint: There are exactly two trees mentioned.

question: Complete the sentence: 'They had to put ___ the school picnic because of the heavy rain.' 🌧️
explanation: Good job! 'Put off' is a phrasal verb that means to postpone or delay an event. ☔
hint: It means to delay to a later date.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Mr. Sharma has been living in this city ___ 2015.' 🏙️
explanation: Superb! 'Since' is used to show the starting point of an action that continues to the present. 🏡
hint: It marks the beginning of a specific time in the past.

question: Select the right preposition: 'The missing ring was found ___ the scattered toys.' 💍
explanation: Excellent! 'Among' is used when something is in the middle of a group of more than two things. 🔍
hint: The toys are a large, uncounted group.

question: Which phrasal verb means to cancel? 'The principal decided to ___ off the meeting.' 🏫
explanation: Awesome! 'Call off' is a common phrasal verb meaning to cancel a planned event. 📋
hint: Think of using a phone to cancel.

question: Fill the blank with a preposition of direction: 'The teacher walked confidently ___ the classroom.' 👩‍🏫
explanation: Brilliant! 'Into' shows movement toward the inside of a closed space. 📚
hint: She moved from outside to inside.

question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Anjali has been studying ___ three continuous hours.' ⏱️
explanation: Perfect! We use 'for' to indicate the duration or length of time an action has been happening. 📖
hint: Three hours is a duration of time.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'Please fasten your seatbelts before the plane takes ___.' ✈️
explanation: Spot on! 'Take off' means to become airborne or leave the ground. ☁️
hint: It describes the moment a plane leaves the runway.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'Come and sit ___ me so we can read together.' 🛋️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Beside' means next to or at the side of someone. 📖
hint: Look for the word that means 'next to' without the 's'.

question: Which word finishes the phrasal verb? 'Our old car tends to break ___ on long trips.' 🚗
explanation: Good job! 'Break down' is used when a machine or vehicle stops functioning. 🔧
hint: It means to stop working.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The puppy ran happily ___ its owner.' 🐕
explanation: Superb! 'Towards' indicates movement in the direction of someone or something. 🎾
hint: It implies getting closer to a target.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Please don\'t bring ___ that embarrassing story again.' 😳
explanation: Excellent! To 'bring up' a topic means to mention it in conversation. 💬
hint: It means to raise a subject.

question: Choose the right preposition: 'My best friend\'s birthday is ___ August.' 🎉
explanation: Awesome! We use 'in' before months, years, and seasons. 🎂
hint: Months use a broad preposition of time.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'I really look forward ___ the upcoming school holidays.' 🏖️
explanation: Brilliant! 'Look forward to' is a three-word phrasal verb meaning to be excited about something in the future. 🚂
hint: This idiom ends with a preposition that indicates direction.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The shy kitten hid ___ the large living room curtains.' 🐱
explanation: Perfect! 'Behind' is a preposition of place meaning at the back of something. 🐾
hint: It is used when something is hiding in the back.

question: Which phrasal verb means to have none left? 'We have run out ___ sugar.' 🍚
explanation: Spot on! 'Run out of' means you have completely used up a supply of something. ☕
hint: It connects the verb 'run out' to the noun 'sugar'.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'Be careful when walking ___ the busy street.' 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Across' means moving from one side of a surface (like a road) to the other. 🛣️
hint: You go from side A to side B on a flat surface.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'She decided to turn ___ the job offer because the pay was low.' 💼
explanation: Good job! To 'turn down' an offer means to reject or refuse it. 📄
hint: It is the opposite of turning something up.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The express train always departs exactly ___ time.' 🚆
explanation: Superb! 'On time' means strictly at the scheduled time, neither late nor early. 🎫
hint: It refers to punctuality.

question: Which word completes the phrasal verb? 'They want to set ___ a new library in our town.' 📚
explanation: Excellent! 'Set up' means to establish, create, or build something new. 🏛️
hint: It means to build or start something.

question: Choose the best preposition: 'The small fishing boat sailed smoothly ___ the bridge.' ⛵
explanation: Awesome! 'Under' implies movement directly below a higher object, like a bridge. 🌊
hint: The boat goes below the structure.

question: Complete the sentence: 'It took me hours to figure ___ the solution to the math problem.' 🧮
explanation: Brilliant! 'Figure out' means to understand or solve something through thought. 🧩
hint: It means to discover the answer.

question: Fill in the blank: 'We took a relaxing stroll ___ the sandy beach.' 🏖️
explanation: Perfect! 'Along' means moving in a line parallel to something long, like a beach or river. 🌊
hint: You walk next to the edge of the water.

question: Which phrasal verb means to arrive? 'He didn\'t show ___ for the basketball game.' 🏀
explanation: Spot on! 'Show up' is a casual phrasal verb meaning to arrive or appear at a place. 🏟️
hint: It means to make an appearance.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'You must submit your science project ___ Friday.' 🔬
explanation: Fantastic! We use 'by' to show a deadline, meaning 'no later than'. 📝
hint: It sets a deadline.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'Feel free to drop ___ whenever you are in the neighborhood.' 🏘️
explanation: Good job! 'Drop in' (or drop by) means to visit informally and unexpectedly. ☕
hint: It means to visit someone inside their house.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Please do not park your car ___ of the main gate.' 🚗
explanation: Superb! 'In front of' is a compound preposition showing spatial relationship directly ahead. 🛑
hint: It means blocking the direct entrance.

question: Which word finishes the phrasal verb? 'Despite the noise, she carried ___ studying for her exams.' 📖
explanation: Excellent! 'Carry on' is a phrasal verb that means to continue doing something. ✍️
hint: It means to continue.

question: Choose the right preposition: 'We have to wait ___ midnight to see the fireworks.' 🎆
explanation: Awesome! 'Until' is used to show continuous action up to a specific point in time. 🎇
hint: It means up to a certain time.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Did you find ___ what time the movie starts?' 🎬
explanation: Brilliant! 'Find out' means to discover information or learn a fact. 🎟️
hint: It means to discover.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Just drive ___ the post office, and you will see the bank.' 🏦
explanation: Perfect! 'Past' as a preposition means to move further than a particular point. 🛣️
hint: It means to go beyond a certain building.

question: Which phrasal verb implies a good relationship? 'I really get ___ well with my elder brother.' 👬
explanation: Spot on! 'Get along' means to have a friendly and harmonious relationship. 😊
hint: It means to coexist nicely.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'Please leave the keys ___ the kitchen table.' 🔑
explanation: Fantastic! 'On' is used when an object is resting on top of a surface. 🏠
hint: It touches the surface.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'Can you hold ___ a minute? I need to tie my shoelaces.' 👟
explanation: Good job! 'Hold on' is commonly used to ask someone to wait for a short time. ⏳
hint: It means to wait.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The grand finale performance starts exactly ___ 5 PM.' 🎭
explanation: Superb! We always use 'at' for specific, precise clock times. 🕰️
hint: Use this for exact hours.

question: Which word completes the phrasal verb? 'It is hard to keep ___ with all the new technology trends.' 💻
explanation: Excellent! 'Keep up' means to move or progress at the same rate as someone or something else. 📱
hint: It means to stay pace with.

question: Choose the best preposition: 'The wet dog jumped ___ of the swimming pool.' 🐕
explanation: Awesome! 'Out of' indicates movement from the inside of a container or space to the outside. 🏊‍♂️
hint: It is a compound preposition denoting an exit.

question: Complete the sentence: 'If you don\'t know the meaning, look it ___ in the dictionary.' 📖
explanation: Brilliant! 'Look up' means to search for information in a reference book or database. 📚
hint: You do this with unknown words.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will be waiting for you ___ the main bus stop.' 🚏
explanation: Perfect! 'At' is used for a specific point or location on a map, like a bus stop. 🚌
hint: It refers to a specific point in space.

question: Which phrasal verb means to invent a story? 'Don\'t believe him; he always makes ___ excuses.' 🤥
explanation: Spot on! To 'make up' something means to invent a story or an excuse, often to deceive. 🎭
hint: It means to fabricate.

question: Select the correct preposition: 'He fell asleep ___ the boring history lecture.' 😴
explanation: Fantastic! 'During' is a preposition used before a noun to say when something happens within a period. 🏫
hint: It is followed by a noun, not a verb.

question: Complete the phrasal verb: 'Please pick ___ your trash before leaving the park.' 🗑️
explanation: Good job! 'Pick up' means to lift something from the ground or a surface. ♻️
hint: It is the opposite of putting something down.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The eagle flew gracefully ___ the towering mountains.' 🦅
explanation: Superb! 'Over' indicates movement across the top of something. ☁️
hint: It flies high above the peaks.

question: Which word finishes the phrasal verb? 'We need to work ___ a solution to this tricky math puzzle.' 🧩
explanation: Excellent! 'Work out' means to solve a problem or calculate an answer. 🧮
hint: It means to figure out a result.
